newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar says "confusion" behind Rasgas rating review.
newsitem.headline: Qatar says "confusion" behind Rasgas rating review.

text.p: Moody's decision to review for possible downgrade the A3 senior secured rating of Ras Laffan LNG Co (Rasgas) bonds resulted from "some confusion" over Rasgas's scrapping of a minimum price provision, the official Qatar News Agency said.

In a report late on Sunday, QNA quoted Finance Ministry Undersecretary Youssef Hussein Kamal as saying: "What has recently been reported about intentions of cutting the rating ...after we eliminated the condition of minimum price provision ...led to some confusion because the picture was not clear to some."
Kamal, who was speaking on the sidelines of gas exhibition in Doha, said Mobil Corp - a partner is Ras Laffan - "would guarantee to the banks the minimum price provision".

On February 25, Moody's Investors Service placed the Rasgas rating under review for possible downgrade following Mobil's announcement regarding the agreement in principle by Rasgas to increase its sales of LNG to the Korea Gas Corp to 4.8 million tonnes a year from 2.4 million and to eliminate the minimum price provision in the sales and purchase agreement.

Moody's said the review would focus on the impact on bondholders of the elimination of the minimum price provision in the S&P agreement, the potential risks and benefits associated with the construction of a second LNG train and the additional debt to be incurred in relation to its construction.
Moody's would also review the form and substance of any additional credit support that Mobil is willing to offer to Ras Laffan lenders.
Rasgas is one of the oil and gas-rich Gulf Arab state's three major gas export projects designed to exploit its mammoth gas reserves - the third largest in the world.
